name: Ahiah
overview: Ahiah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as a non-Levite leader. He is specifically named on the sealed document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, appearing in verse 26. His role as a leader outside the Levitical tribe highlights his distinct position among the community leaders during this period.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahiah means '[my] brother is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 10:26 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Ahiah as a descendant of Jacob, establishing his Israelite heritage as noted in Nehemiah 10:26. No other family relationships are recorded for him beyond this lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Ahiah's mention on the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah 10:26 underscores his involvement in the community's commitment to follow God's law during the post-exilic restoration. As a non-Levite leader, his inclusion demonstrates the broader leadership structure beyond the Levitical priesthood in the rebuilding of Israel's religious and social order. His role contributes to the collective responsibility embraced by the people in renewing their covenant with God.
